newsitem.title: UK: BP, OSG discuss Alaska tanker deal.
newsitem.headline: BP, OSG discuss Alaska tanker deal.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc is discussing with New York-based Overseas Shipholding Group (OSG) plans to build new tankers to replace its ageing fleet lifting Alaskan crude, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.

The spokesman for BP Shipping USA said the company "has reached an agreement to work with OSG to consider options that are available, driven by the need to replace the single hull vessels in the Alaskan crude oil trade."
The spokesman, in Cleveland, Ohio, declined to say how many new vessels may be built or how many ships would be replaced, saying such information was commercially sensitive.
He said the ships would be built in the U.S. and be manned by U.S. crews, as required under the Jones Act affecting vessels sailing between American ports.

He said most of BP's fleet currently employed lifting Alaskan crude had been in service since the 1970s. Such vessels are being phased out following the 1990 Oil Pollution Act, introduced after the 1989 Exxon Valdez oil spill.
Officials from OSG were not immediately available for comment.
